event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: KO’s 2021 Form 10-K squarely links COVID-19 to multiple, already-realised hits on revenue, operations and supply chains while warning that many of these pressures could intensify.  The disclosure is recent (within one year of the filing) and is therefore subject to minimal time-decay.  The language is specific rather than boiler-plate: management cites concrete impacts—such as global sales declines, acute weakness in away-from-home channels, production outages, delayed concentrate shipments, container shortages, remote-work productivity risks, legal exposure and possible asset impairments.  These are not hypothetical scenarios; they are described as events that “have had” negative effects with the expectation they “will continue.”  Although the company lists mitigating steps (portfolio focus, marketing shifts, health measures), these are framed as uncertain in effectiveness.  Taken together, the evidence portrays a high-severity, continuing risk environment, warranting elevated snippet scores (7–9) under the Time Decay Principle for an event less than three years old.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has had, and we expect will continue to have, certain negative impacts on our business, and such impacts have had, and may continue to have, a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

components.reason: Explicitly states past and continuing negative impacts tied directly to COVID-19.
Uses strong materiality language ('material adverse effect').
Covers multiple financial dimensions (results, condition, cash-flows).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct linkage to pandemic, confirmed materiality and multi-facet impact justify a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced a decrease in sales of certain of our products in markets around the world as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Describes an actual, quantified-in-effect sales decline, not just potential.
Global scope ('around the world') increases severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete worldwide sales drop attributable to COVID-19 merits a strong but slightly lower score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Sales of our products in the away-from-home channels have been significantly negatively affected by shelter-in-place regulations or recommendations, closings of restaurants and cancellations of major sporting and other events that were imposed as a result of the initial COVID-19 outbreak.

components.reason: Specifies magnitude ('significantly') and channel most impacted.
Links causation to government measures tied to pandemic.
Highlights demand-side vulnerability (channel concentration).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed channel impact with explicit COVID-19 causation scores a solid 6.

evidence_list.snippet: If COVID-19 infection trends increase, the pandemic intensifies or expands geographically or efforts to curb the pandemic are ineffective, the negative impacts of the pandemic on our sales could be more prolonged and may become more severe.

components.reason: Forward-looking escalation risk identified.
Highlights potential for extended duration and severity.
Conditional wording reduces immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential rather than realised impact, with conditional tone, yields a moderate score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: In certain COVID-19 affected markets, consumer demand has shifted away from some of our more profitable beverages and away-from-home consumption to lower-margin products and at-home consumption, and this shift in consumer purchasing patterns is likely to continue while shelter-in-place and social distancing behaviors are mandated or encouraged.

components.reason: Shows margin compression through mix shift, a direct profitability threat.
Indicates persistence of the trend ('likely to continue').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes an ongoing, profitability-eroding demand shift; earns a mid-high score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced temporary disruptions in certain of our concentrate production operations.

components.reason: Operational disruption already realised.
Pertains to core production (concentrate); critical supply-chain node.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Realised disruptions at production level pose tangible risk, justifying a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We have faced, and may continue to face, delays in the delivery of concentrates to our bottling partners as a result of shipping delays due to, among other things, additional safety requirements imposed by port authorities, closures of or congestion at ports, and capacity constraints experienced by our transportation contractors.

components.reason: Details multiple logistics choke-points causing delivery delays.
States both realised and future exposure ('have faced, and may continue to face').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific, multi-factor supply-chain delays elevate operational risk to a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Disruptions in supply chains have placed, and may continue to place, constraints on our and our bottling partners' ability to source beverage containers, such as glass bottles and cans, which has increased, and in the future may increase, our and their packaging costs.

components.reason: Explicit mention of supply-chain disruption affecting critical inputs.
Quantifies financial consequence (higher packaging costs).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Container shortages with cost inflation risk merit a score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We may experience reductions in productivity and disruptions to our business routines while our remote work policy remains in place.

components.reason: Highlights internal operational risk from remote-work transition.
Prospective, not yet quantified or realised.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential internal efficiency risk is noted but unquantified; scores a low 1.

evidence_list.snippet: Any of the negative impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, including those described above, alone or in combination with others, may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

components.reason: Summarises multiple pandemic impacts leading to material adverse effect.
Covers comprehensive financial metrics (operations, condition, cash).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Catch-all materiality statement consolidates risk significance; earns a 5.
